title: Indian Market News Brief — 04 Nov 2026 — Nifty 50
quick_read: Strong buying by foreign funds and solid quarterly profits from large private banks and SBI may support the market. On the other hand, crude oil prices climbing above 105 dollars and US bond yields approaching 5 percent could create pressure on local shares. How global markets react to the US midterm election results and Middle East tensions remains unclear.

stories.headline: FPIs pour Rs 21,715 crore into Indian stocks in 10 days; is record sell-off finally reversing?
stories.summary:
Foreign portfolio investors put 21,715 crore rupees into Indian shares over a span of 10 days.
This inflow equals approximately 2.29 billion US dollars.
The purchases mark an improvement in sentiment after previous heavy selling by overseas funds.
Market observers noted support from firm company profits and attractive prices.
stories.impact: May help Nifty: Heavy purchases by foreign investors bring fresh cash into big index stocks and can lift overall share prices.

stories.headline: US Treasury yields climb as strong jobs data, midterm polls weigh; 10-year yield eyes 5% again
stories.summary:
US government bond yields moved higher following stronger than expected jobs data in America.
The 10-year US bond yield moved back toward the 5 percent mark.
Investors are waiting for the final results of the US midterm elections.
A firm US job market suggests that American interest rates may stay high for longer.
stories.impact: May hurt Nifty: High returns on safe US government bonds can pull foreign money out of Indian shares.

stories.headline: Markets extend gains for fourth day; FPI buying highest in a year
stories.summary:
Indian benchmark indices advanced for a fourth consecutive day.
Brent crude oil prices rose 2 percent during trading to reach 105.29 dollars per barrel.
Crude prices had slipped earlier before recovering sharply.
Gains in the domestic market were led by consumer goods and financial firms.
stories.impact: May hurt Nifty: Costlier crude oil increases fuel import bills for India and can squeeze profit margins for paint, tyre, and transport companies.

stories.headline: Loan growth, fall in provisions help SBI profits in Q2
stories.summary:
State Bank of India posted a 14 percent rise in second-quarter net profit to 23,038 crore rupees.
Total lending by the bank expanded by 18 percent compared to last year.
The bank benefited from higher net interest earnings and reduced deposit expenses.
Provisions kept aside to cover bad loans were lower than in the prior year.
stories.impact: May help Nifty: Better profit and steady loan growth at the nation's biggest state-run lender could improve sentiment for the banking sector.

stories.headline: Reliance shares see volume breakout: Is a trend reversal around the corner? Here’s what RIL stock history shows
stories.summary:
Reliance Industries shares surged nearly 12 percent in a single trading session on November 2.
The jump added almost 2 lakh crore rupees to the company total market value.
Trading took place with unusually high volume.
Market participants pointed to stable quarterly figures and progress at its telecom unit.
stories.impact: May help Nifty: Because Reliance carries the heaviest weight in the index, its strength can directly pull the Nifty higher.

stories.headline: Nifty Private Bank index gains 2%; HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Axis Bank shine
stories.summary:
The Nifty Private Bank index gained 2 percent during recent market action.
HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank each rallied 7 percent across five trading days.
These gains exceeded the 5 percent increase seen in the broader Nifty 50 over the same time.
Axis Bank also recorded strong buying interest from investors.
stories.impact: May help Nifty: Private lenders account for a very large portion of the index, so their price rise strongly supports the market.

stories.headline: RBI to conduct Overnight Variable Rate Reverse Repo (VRRR) auction under LAF on November 04, 2026
stories.summary:
The Reserve Bank of India decided to hold an auction to temporarily absorb 50,000 crore rupees from banks.
This Variable Rate Reverse Repo auction will take place on November 4, 2026.
The funds taken from banks will be returned on November 5, 2026.
The central bank took this step after studying current cash levels across the banking system.
stories.impact: Little effect on Nifty: This is a routine one-day operation by the central bank to manage short-term cash in banks and rarely affects stock prices.

stories.headline: RBI eases forex rules for services exports and imports
stories.summary:
The Reserve Bank of India relaxed foreign exchange rules for service exports and imports.
The amended rules are effective from October 1, 2026.
Resident individuals who export services will benefit from simpler self-declarations.
The changes aim to make cross-border transactions faster and reduce paperwork.
stories.impact: May help Nifty: Simpler compliance for international payments can lower administrative hassles for software and consulting exporters.

stories.headline: Rupee nudges higher, forward premiums dip with focus on US midterm, oil moves
stories.summary:
The Indian rupee settled slightly higher at 94.74 per US dollar on Tuesday.
Currency markets focused on the counting of votes in the US midterm elections.
Developments around the conflict in Iran also kept currency traders watchful.
A recovery in global oil prices capped further gains for the rupee.
stories.impact: Unclear for Nifty: A steady currency helps keep import bills manageable, but rising oil prices and overseas war risks may restrain gains.

stories.headline: NSE Q2 Results: Profit jumps 23% to Rs 2,578 crore, revenue rises 9%
stories.summary:
National Stock Exchange of India reported a 23 percent increase in second-quarter profit to 2,578 crore rupees.
Total revenue rose 9 percent over the year.
Profit after tax in the same quarter last year was 2,098 crore rupees.
The exchange gained from active trading across cash and derivative segments.
stories.impact: May help Nifty: Strong growth at the primary stock exchange reflects healthy participation and activity across the broader capital market.

stories.headline: European shares fall as tech stocks slide, Middle East tensions weigh
stories.summary:
European stock indices dropped as technology company shares faced selling pressure.
Global investors showed concern over high valuations among artificial intelligence businesses.
Tensions between the US and Iran weighed on general trading mood in Europe.
Higher oil prices added to worries for European companies.
stories.impact: May hurt Nifty: Selling in global technology shares and geopolitical tension overseas could prompt cautious trading in Indian IT firms.

stories.headline: Margin trading facility position value declines after 6 months of growth
stories.summary:
The value of borrowed funds used by traders to buy shares fell 4.65 percent in October to 1.44 trillion rupees.
This drop ended five straight months of rising margin trading positions.
Exchange data showed that retail and institutional traders trimmed their borrowed exposures.
Investors chose to reduce leverage after recent market fluctuations.

stories.headline: Sugar Slides to Five-Week Low as High Indian Output Jolts Market
stories.summary:
Global sugar prices fell to their lowest point in five weeks.
Data revealed that Indian sugar production is running well ahead of last year pace.
Futures contracts have fallen more than 13 percent from their previous month high.
Higher supply from Indian farms has increased total availability in world markets.
stories.impact: May hurt Nifty: Weaker international prices could reduce the earnings and profit margins of Indian sugar manufacturers.
